 Judgment
Respondent No.2- insurer in M.V.C.No.143/2007 on the file of the Additional M.A.C.T., & Fast Track Court - II, Koppal (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal')

is impugning the judgment and award dated 30.07.2011 awarding the compensation of Rs.4,22,710/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization and directing respondent 2 to deposit the compensation amount within two months.

The parties are referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal, for the sake of convenience.
2.

Brief facts of the case are that the claimant filed the claim petition against respondent Nos.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the truck bearing Reg.No.KA-16/15 claiming compensation for the injuries suffered by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

3. It is contended by the claimant that on 02.02.2006 at 09:40 PM he was riding the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.M-8-,CTR-8733 and at the same time, the NC: 2023:KHC-D:7466 driver of the truck bearing Reg.No.KA-16/15 driven the same in a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the two wheeler ridden by the claimant, as a result of which, he sustained grievous injuries including fracture of right tibia.
Immediately, he was shifted to the Government Hospital at Koppal and thereafter to KIMS Hospital, Hubli, where he took treatment as an inpatient for about 60 days.
The claimant has incurred huge amount towards medical expenses.
Respondents being the insured and insurer of the truck in question are liable to pay the compensation.
Accordingly, prayed for allowing the claim petition.
4. Respondent No.1 has not contested the matter.
Respondent No.2 filed objection statement denying the contentions of the claimant and his entitlement to get the compensation.
It is denied that the driver of the truck in question has driven the same in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident.
It is contended that the claimant himself was negligent and he who has caused the accident.

Therefore, respondent No.2 prayed for dismissal of the claimant petition.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7466 5.

During the pendency of the claim petition, the claimant died and his legal representatives were brought on record as petitioner Nos.1(A) to 1(E).
6.

On the basis of these pleadings, the following issues were came to be framed;
"1.

Whether the petitioner Andappa died due to accidental injuries in the accident on 02-02-2006 at about 9.40 P.M., on N.H-63 Road, near Old D.C.Office Circle due to rash & negligent driving of Lorry bearing No.KA- 16/15?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so how much and, from whom?

7. The wife of the claimant is examined as PW1 and she examined PW2 and got marked Exs.P1 to 61 in support of her contentions.
Respondent No.2 got examined RW1 and got marked Ex.R1 in support of its defence.

8. The trail Court after taking into consideration all these materials on record, came to the conclusion that the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.4,22,710/-, accordingly, directed respondent No.2 to pay the compensation.
Being aggrieved by the same, respondent No.2 is before this Court.

10. Heard Sri. A.G.Jadhav, learned counsel for the appellant- insurer and Sri. Hanumanthareddy Sahukar, learned counsel for respondent Nos.3 to 5- claimants.
11.
Learned counsel for the appellant contended that it is the specific contention of the claimant that he suffered fracture of right tibia and fibula and undertaken treatment for some days.
The accident had occurred on 02.02.2006 and the claim petition was came to be filed on 30.03.2007.
By that time, he has already undergone necessary treatment, but he died on 30.03.2008.
The cause of death is not known, there is no post mortem examination report.
Therefore there is no nexus between the injury and the cause of death of the claimant.
Under such circumstances, the Tribunal committed an error in awarding the compensation.
Accordingly, he prays for dismissal of the claim petition.

Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent Nos.1(A) to 1(E) being the legal representatives of the original claimant opposing the appeal submitted that the claimant had suffered grievous injuries.
He undertook treatment continuously in various hospitals and spent huge amount.
In spite of that he died.
Under such circumstances, the Tribunal was right in awarding the compensation.
He also contended that the claimants have already withdrawn 50% of the award amount deposited by the appellant- insurer.
Under such circumstances, there is no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.
13. Perused the materials on record.

14. In view of the above, the point that would arise of consideration is;
 Whether the impugned judgment and  award passed by the Tribunal requires  interference of this Court?

sentences.text:
My answer to the above point is partly in the affirmative for the following;
REASONS 16.
The claimant in the claim petition categorically stated that he has suffered fracture of right leg and had taken treatment at KIMS Hospital, Hubli.
Ex.P7 is the wound certificate issued at District Hospital, Koppal according to which the claimant suffered as many as 6 injuries.
The X-ray shows fracture of upper end of right tibia involving both the candezla and head fibula.
Therefore injury No.4 was considered to be the grievous injury and the other injuries are simple in nature.
Ex.P8 is the medical certificate issued by the KIMS Hospital, Hubli according to which the injured admitted to the hospital on 03.02.2006 and was discharged on 03.04.2006.
The extensive investigation done during this period evidence the fracture of upper end of right tibia involving head of fibula.
Ex.P9 is the patient discharge card issued by the KIMS Hospital, Hubli which corresponds with Ex.P8 regarding treating the claimant as inpatient from 03.02.20006 to 03.04.2006.

Ex.P10 is the another discharge NC: 2023:KHC-D:7466 card issued by the KIMS Hospital, Hubli according to which the claimant has once again admitted to the hospital on 15.06.2006 and was discharged on 05.07.2006.
Exs.P13 to 43 are the medical bills totaling to Rs.2,710/- apart from this, there are no other medical records that could be taken into consideration.

17. Even if all the above documents which are placed before the Court are taken into consideration,
accept holding that the claimant has spent Rs.2,710/- for his treatment, there is nothing on record to suggest that the death of the claimant was due to the injuries suffered by him in the road traffic accident.
As rightly contended by the appellant, there is no nexus between the injuries sustained in the accident and the cause of death.
Under such circumstances, the claimants are not entitled for compensation accept under the head of medical expenses.
As per the medical bills, the claimant has spent Rs.2,710/-.
Therefore, it could be held that the claimants are entitled for medical expenses of Rs.3,000/-, but they are not entitled for any compensation under any other head.
The Tribunal has not taken into consideration all these aspects of the matter, but proceeded to award huge amount as compensation.
The reasons assigned by the Tribunal for awarding compensation is not acceptable.

In para No. 12 of the impugned judgment, the Tribunal observes that in all the decisions referred by it, a guideline is issued that if the injured dies, the claimants have to establish the nexus between the injury and the cause of death, then only the dependents can claim compensation.
It also observed that no post mortem report is produced in the present case.
The death was occurred about 1 and half years after the accident.

It also categorically observed that The Divisional Manager, United India ... vs Andappa S/O Shettappa Hadimani on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38274292/
5 it is difficult to hold that the death is the direct cause of the injuries sustained in the accident, but however it concluded by saying that "But anyhow, under the conventional heads the petitioners are entitled to get compensation".

sentences.text: This finding of the Tribunal cannot be accepted as the same is erroneous and without any basis.

Hence, the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is to be modified to hold that the claimants are entitled for compensation of only - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7466 Rs.3,000/- towards medical expenses.

Accordingly, I answer the above point partly in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following;
ORDER 1) The appeal is allowed in part.
2) The impugned judgment and award dated 30.07.2011 passed in M.V.C.No.143/2007 on the file of the Additional M.A.C.T., & Fast Track Court - II, Koppal is modified.
It is held that the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.3,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit of the amount.
Amount in deposit in access to the amount awarded is ordered to be refunded to the appellant- insurer on due identification.

It is brought to the notice of the Court that the major portion of the award amount is deposited before this Court and the sum of Rs.1,62,241/- along with interest accrued on - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7466 the fixed deposit is transmitted to the Tribunal.
The Tribunal is directed to appropriate and pay the compensation that is due to the claimants and refund the balance amount to the insurer on due identification.
